title: Signed CellComplex: ℤ-Valued Sign with Interior-Door Cancellation
description: Answers OQ-04 of sperner-ndim-mathlib-oq-01: generalize the abstract CellComplex framework to signed cell complexes (oriented chains). Adjacent facets carry opposite ±1 signs satisfying the coherence sign(s,k) + sign(s',k') = 0. The signed-interior-doors theorem shows the sum of facet signs over interior doors vanishes in ℤ, via Finset.sum_involution applied to the lifted adjacency map. The naive ZMod-2-valued sign with sum-to-one coherence is shown to be mathematically vacuous (collapses to a Bool-valued labeling under ZMod.neg_eq_self_mod_two); ℤ is the right ground ring for orientation tracking.

originalContributions: SignedCellComplex: structure extending CellComplex with per-facet ℤ-valued ±1 sign field and sign_adj coherence (adjacent facets sum to 0)
signedAdjMap: lift of the parent's adjacency map to the signed signature
signedDoorCount: signed door count (sum of facet signs over door facets, in ℤ)
signed_interior_doors_sum_zero: the sum of facet signs over interior doors vanishes in ℤ — signed analog of the parent's interior_doors_even, discharged via Finset.sum_involution
sign_ne_zero: facet signs are never zero (immediate from sign_pm_one)

overview.historicalContext:
The unsigned door-counting argument formalised in the parent `SpernerNDimMathlib.lean` works over `ZMod 2` parity: interior doors cancel pairwise mod 2, and the boundary-door count detects fully-coloured cells. To lift this to signed (oriented) chain complexes — needed for the equivariant generalisations Tucker's lemma and Borsuk–Ulam — one would naïvely add a `ZMod 2`-valued sign field with a `sign s k + sign s' k' = 1` coherence on adjacent facets, intending 'opposite signs'. This file diagnoses that approach as **mathematically vacuous**: in `ZMod 2`, every element satisfies `-a = a` (Mathlib's `ZMod.neg_eq_self_mod_two`), so 'opposite signs' degenerates to 'differs-on-adjacency', and the would-be signed-cancellation theorem reduces to the parent's unsigned even-count statement. The classical signed-chain boundary `∂σ = ∑ (-1)^i ∂_i σ` lives over ℤ (or any field of characteristic ≠ 2); in `ℤ/2` it collapses to the unsigned boundary.

This file implements the **ℤ-valued** signed cell complex: per-facet `±1` signs with `sign s k + sign s' k' = 0` (i.e., genuinely opposite in ℤ). The signed-interior-doors cancellation theorem then closes directly via Mathlib's `Finset.sum_involution` (lemma added by the Mathlib community as the additive cousin of `Finset.prod_involution`). The discharge mirrors the parent's `interior_doors_even` proof: the same `adjMap` involution structure is reused, with the parent's three adjacency axioms (`adj_symm`, `adj_vertices`, `adj_ne`) supplying involution / membership preservation / fixed-point-freeness, and `sign_adj` supplying the cancellation hypothesis `f a + f (g a) = 0`.

The motivation is structural: a signed `CellComplex` is the natural Lean-side substrate for a future Tucker's lemma formalisation (antipodal ℤ/2-equivariant Sperner) and for bridging the abstract `CellComplex` API to Mathlib's `AlternatingFaceMapComplex` over `ModuleCat ℤ`. This file delivers the structural definition + the foundational cancellation theorem in 200 LOC with 0 axioms and 0 sorries, leaving the Tucker/Borsuk–Ulam bridges as separate follow-up sessions.
overview.problemStatement: Generalize the abstract CellComplex framework (sperner-ndim-mathlib) to signed cell complexes: enrich each cell complex with a per-facet ℤ-valued ±1 sign field satisfying sign(s,k) + sign(s',k') = 0 for adjacent facets. Prove the signed analog of interior_doors_even: ∑_{(s,k) interior door} sign(s,k) = 0 in ℤ.
overview.text: Proves that adjacent-facet sign cancellation in a signed cell complex yields a vanishing signed-door sum over interior doors, discharging via Finset.sum_involution.
overview.proofStrategy: 1. Define SignedCellComplex extending CellComplex with sign : Simplex → Fin (d+1) → ℤ, sign_pm_one (±1 valuation), and sign_adj (adjacent sum = 0). 2. Define signedAdjMap as the lifted adjacency map and signedDoorCount as the sum of facet signs over door facets. 3. For signed_interior_doors_sum_zero: restrict to S = {(s,k) | door ∧ adj ≠ none}; apply Finset.sum_involution with g := λp _hp => signedAdjMap p; verify the four obligations (cancellation = sign_adj, fixed-point-freeness = adj_ne, membership preservation = door_transfer + adj_symm, involution = adj_symm).
keyInsights: ZMod 2 is the wrong ground ring for orientation tracking: ZMod.neg_eq_self_mod_two collapses opposite signs to identical signs, making the 'signed' structure degenerate to the unsigned parent.
The right coherence for adjacent facets is sign(s,k) + sign(s',k') = 0 in ℤ (i.e., they are genuinely negatives), which makes ∂σ = ∑ (-1)^i ∂_i σ a meaningful boundary operator.

Finset.sum_involution (additive cousin of prod_involution, derived via @[to_additive]) is the ideal Mathlib hammer: it takes a dependent involution g : ∀ a ∈ s, ι with a cancellation hypothesis f a + f (g a ha) = 0 and yields ∑ x ∈ s, f x = 0 directly.

The parent's interior_doors_even proof structure (using adjMap as the involution and the three CellComplex adjacency axioms) reuses verbatim for the signed cancellation, modulo replacing the parity-of-cardinality conclusion with the additive-zero conclusion.

The parent's door_transfer lemma is private, so the signed file re-proves a one-dir variant (door_transfer_signed_one_dir, 8 LOC) directly from the public adj_vertices axiom. No parent surgery is needed.

The `structure ... extends CellComplex` design (rather than bundling a parent field) is the right Lean 4 idiom: the autogenerated `K.toCellComplex` projection lets every `SignedCellComplex` inherit the parent's API (adj_symm, adj_vertices, adj_ne, isDoorAt, doorCount) without re-declaration — the standard Mathlib pattern for adding orientation, grading, or filtration data to an existing combinatorial structure.
prerequisites: SpernerNDimMathlib (abstract CellComplex with adj_symm, adj_vertices, adj_ne axioms)
openQuestions: Bridge to Mathlib's AlternatingFaceMapComplex over ModuleCat ℤ: embed SignedCellComplex into a chain complex with the standard signed boundary operator.
Tucker's lemma: state and prove the antipodal ℤ/2-equivariant Sperner statement over an Antipodal variant of SignedCellComplex (vertex-level involution ι : V → V with ι_involutive + ι_no_fp).
Borsuk–Ulam: derive the topological consequence from the signed cancellation theorem via the standard reduction to antipodal sphere maps.

sections.title: Signed Interior Doors Sum to Zero
sections.summary: `signed_interior_doors_sum_zero`: the central cancellation theorem. Applies `Finset.sum_involution` with the four obligations dispatched in named case blocks (cancel / fpf / gmem / invol). Mirrors the parent's `interior_doors_even` skeleton but yields an additive-zero conclusion in ℤ instead of an even-cardinality conclusion.

conclusion.summary: Delivers a structural ℤ-valued signed CellComplex and the foundational signed-interior-doors cancellation theorem (sum vanishes in ℤ) in 207 LOC with 0 axioms and 0 sorries. The ZMod-2-vacuity diagnosis (sign collapse via ZMod.neg_eq_self_mod_two) justifies the move to ℤ, and Finset.sum_involution discharges the cancellation directly.
conclusion.implications: This is the substrate for two follow-up directions: (1) embedding into Mathlib's AlternatingFaceMapComplex over ModuleCat ℤ to connect with the standard algebraic-topology API, and (2) the Tucker/Borsuk–Ulam chain — Tucker's lemma is the antipodal ℤ/2-equivariant Sperner statement, and the ℤ-valued sign structure here is exactly the orientation data needed for the equivariant counting argument. The 207-LOC delivery preserves the proof economy of the parent's abstract framework: no concrete triangulation is required, the three CellComplex adjacency axioms suffice for the signed cancellation. Notably, the four Finset.sum_involution obligations align bijectively with the four CellComplex+Signed axioms (cancel↔sign_adj, fpf↔adj_ne, gmem↔adj_vertices+adj_symm, invol↔adj_symm), evidencing a tight axiomatisation with no redundancy for this theorem.

The signed CellComplex structure here is the natural ℤ-valued substrate for an equivariant Sperner argument; Tucker's lemma (the ℤ/2-equivariant Sperner statement) is the combinatorial heart of Borsuk–Ulam. This file delivers the foundational cancellation theorem; the Tucker/Borsuk–Ulam bridges remain follow-up work.

The Sperner → Brouwer reduction relies on the unsigned door-counting parity argument; the signed (oriented) analog here is the natural lift for an *equivariant* Brouwer statement (degree-tracking via the ℤ-valued sign field). The signed-interior-doors cancellation theorem is the structural ingredient that would feed any such oriented refinement.

Mathlib4's concrete Sperner formalisation operates over a specific geometric triangulation; this file's abstract signed CellComplex is the orientation-aware companion to the parent's abstract unsigned framework. The two stacks are complementary: Mathlib4-Sperner gives a concrete combinatorial closed theorem; the abstract framework here gives the structural API for equivariant / signed extensions.

mainTheorems.name: SignedCellComplex
mainTheorems.statement: $\mathrm{SignedCellComplex}\ V\ d := \mathrm{CellComplex}\ V\ d \text{ extended with } \{\mathrm{sign} : \mathrm{Simplex} \to \mathrm{Fin}(d{+}1) \to \mathbb{Z},\ \mathrm{sign\_pm\_one},\ \mathrm{sign\_adj}\}$
mainTheorems.significance: The structural definition: enriches the parent's abstract `CellComplex` with a per-facet ℤ-valued ±1 sign field and the adjacency-orientation coherence `sign s k + sign s' k' = 0`. This is the right framework for orientation-aware combinatorial topology (Tucker's lemma, Borsuk–Ulam, signed chain complexes).
mainTheorems.description: Signed cell complex structure. Extends `CellComplex V d` with `sign : Simplex → Fin (d+1) → ℤ`, `sign_pm_one : sign ∈ {±1}`, and `sign_adj : adj s k = some (s', k') → sign s k + sign s' k' = 0`.

mainTheorems.name: signedAdjMap
mainTheorems.statement: $\mathrm{signedAdjMap}\ K\ p := \begin{cases} (s',k') & K.\mathrm{adj}\ p_1\ p_2 = \mathrm{some}\ (s',k') \\ p & K.\mathrm{adj}\ p_1\ p_2 = \mathrm{none} \end{cases}$
mainTheorems.significance: The lifted adjacency map: at an interior facet, follow the parent's adjacency; at a boundary facet, stay put. Identical in form to the parent's `private adjMap`, lifted to a public name for use in the signed cancellation theorem.
mainTheorems.description: Signed adjacency map on `K.Simplex × Fin (d+1)`. Match on `K.adj p.1 p.2` and return the paired facet or fall through to the original at boundary.

mainTheorems.name: signedDoorCount
mainTheorems.statement: $\mathrm{signedDoorCount}\ K\ c := \sum_{(s,k)\ :\ \mathrm{isDoorAt}\ c\ K\ s\ k} K.\mathrm{sign}\ s\ k$
mainTheorems.significance: The signed door count: sum of facet signs over door facets (in ℤ). Together with the signed-interior-doors-sum-zero theorem, this isolates the boundary-door contribution to the signed count, mirroring the parent's unsigned parity split.
mainTheorems.description: Signed door count: ∑ K.sign s k over facets (s,k) satisfying isDoorAt c K s k. Lives in ℤ.

mainTheorems.name: signed_interior_doors_sum_zero
mainTheorems.statement: $\forall K,\ c,\ \sum_{(s,k)\ :\ \mathrm{isDoorAt}\ c\ K\ s\ k \land K.\mathrm{adj}\ s\ k \ne \mathrm{none}} K.\mathrm{sign}\ s\ k = 0$
mainTheorems.significance: **The headline cancellation result.** The sum of facet signs over interior doors vanishes in ℤ. Discharged directly via `Finset.sum_involution` applied to `signedAdjMap`, with cancellation supplied by `sign_adj`. This is the signed analog of the parent's `interior_doors_even` (cardinality is even).
mainTheorems.description: Signed interior-door cancellation. Apply Finset.sum_involution with g := λ p _hp => signedAdjMap K p. Four obligations: cancellation (sign_adj), fixed-point-freeness for nonzero values (adj_ne), domain preservation (door_transfer_signed_one_dir + adj_symm), and involution (adj_symm).

references.relevance: Provides `sum_involution` as the additive cousin of `prod_involution` via @[to_additive]. The dependent-argument signature (`g : ∀ a ∈ s, ι`) is the precise shape we need for the signed cancellation discharge.
The vacuity witness: `∀ a : ZMod 2, -a = a` is the precise lemma that collapses 'opposite signs' to 'identical signs' in ZMod 2, justifying the move to ℤ-valued signs.

references.citation: Matoušek, J. (2008). Using the Borsuk-Ulam Theorem. Springer.
references.relevance: Standard reference for the equivariant / antipodal versions of Sperner's lemma (Tucker, Ky Fan, KKM equivariant). Chapter 2 details the signed counting argument that this file's signed_interior_doors_sum_zero theorem foundationally supports.

references.citation: Hatcher, A. (2002). Algebraic Topology. Cambridge University Press. §2.1 (Simplicial and Singular Homology).
references.relevance: Standard reference for oriented simplicial chain complexes with the alternating-sign boundary operator $\partial \sigma = \sum_i (-1)^i \partial_i \sigma$. The ℤ-valued sign field of `SignedCellComplex` is the abstract-CellComplex analogue of Hatcher's per-facet orientation data; the signed-interior-doors cancellation theorem here mirrors the $\partial \circ \partial = 0$ identity over a single facet pair. Hatcher's discussion of why characteristic ≠ 2 matters for orientation is the textbook companion to this file's ZMod-2-vacuity diagnosis.
